strings.name: Jeanne Gang
strings.role: Architect · Founding partner of Studio Gang
strings.summary: Gang draws on ecological systems to connect structure, materials and how people meet. She founded Studio Gang, expanding from the Aqua residential tower to museums, campuses and parks. The Art of Architectural Grafting proposes additions and reuse as ways to extend existing buildings. She also teaches at Harvard and received the 2026 Thomas Jefferson Foundation Medal in Architecture.

strings.influence.rationale: Combines structure, ecology and social interaction in projects such as Aqua, advancing discussion of towers and public space.
strings.facts.f1.label: Birthplace
strings.facts.f2.label: Education
strings.facts.f2.value: BS from the University of Illinois; Harvard architecture master's in 1993; also studied at ETH Zurich.
strings.highlights.h1.title: Towers and neighborly relations
strings.highlights.h1.text: Aqua's undulating balconies shape its exterior while making outdoor residential space central to the tower.
strings.highlights.h2.title: Public architecture and ecology
strings.highlights.h2.text: Projects including the Gilder Center combine spatial connections, public activity and material exploration.
strings.timeline.t1.title: Received the Jefferson architecture medal
strings.timeline.t1.text: Accepted the award at UVA and discussed architecture's support for shared knowledge and exchange.
strings.timeline.t2.title: Became Harvard's Kajima professor
strings.timeline.t2.text: The practice professorship continued her teaching on materials, reuse and the environment.
strings.timeline.t3.title: Published a book on architectural grafting
strings.timeline.t3.text: The Art of Architectural Grafting explored strategies for adding to and transforming existing buildings.
strings.timeline.t4.title: Gilder Center opened
strings.timeline.t4.text: The American Museum of Natural History's new center uses connected spaces for science education and public activity.
strings.timeline.t5.title: Received a MacArthur fellowship
strings.timeline.t5.text: Her combination of design, social questions and environmental concerns gained interdisciplinary recognition.
strings.timeline.t6.title: Aqua became a Chicago landmark
strings.timeline.t6.text: Undulating slabs and balconies gave the residential tower a distinctive identity and made it a signature project.
strings.timeline.t7.title: Founded Studio Gang
strings.timeline.t7.text: Established the Chicago practice, gradually developing international architecture and urban design work.
strings.timeline.t8.title: Completed Harvard's architecture master's
strings.timeline.t8.text: Earned the degree after earlier study and practice, building foundations for independent work.
